newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan single-family home sales rose 8.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan single-family home sales rose 8.6 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, with percent changes from prior months (numbers in 1,000s).
- Pct----Jan Dec--Rev from Nov--Rev from
-By Region: Pct----Jan Dec--Rev from Nov--Rev from
Total January sales of single-family homes rose 19.7 percent from an annualized rate of 727,000 units a year ago.
In 1,000s: Jan Dec--Rev from Nov--Rev from
Actual Units Sold 64 51 51 55 55
Note-Actual number of new single-family units sold is not seasonally adjusted.
Wall Street economists had expected January single-family home sales at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 757,000 units.
The department also revised monthly percent changes of total sales, seasonally adjusted, from prior months as follows:
- Dec-Rev from Nov--Rev from Oct--Rev from
The annualized sales rate for October was revised to 706,000 units from 672,000.
The January supply of homes for sale fell to 4.5 months' worth from a revised 5.0 months' worth in December. December was previously reported at 5.2 months.
The inventory of houses for sale at the end of January was 314,000 units, down from a revised 322,000 units in December. December was previously reported at 327,000 units.

The department said more than half of the new-home sales data were collected with the use of a computerized technology which it said appears to add an upward bias to the estimates. But it said it will adopt procedures to "dampen monthly fluctuations" in the estimates until the impact of the transition is fully understood.

The 63.4 percent rise in January sales in the Northeast was the biggest jump since a 92 percent surge in April 1993 and the Northeast sales rate of 134,000 units in January was the highest since a rate of 152,000 units in November 1987, it said.
It said the January monthly supply of 4.5 months' worth of homes for sale was the lowest since there were also 4.5 months on hand in December 1993.
The overall new-home sales rate of 870,000 units in January was the highest since a rate of 880,000 units in March 1986, the department said.
In the South, the January sales rate of 403,000 units was the highest since 440,000 units in December 1983, it said.
